upper_bound.quote: (standard; details omitted). In all cases $G_p$ is invariant. $\blacksquare$
upper_bound.witness: Missing statement: for all nonnegative integers α, β and every positive integer t, (t | α and t | β) iff (t | min(α,β) and t | |α−β|), and hence the set of common divisors of the full N-tuple of p-adic valuations is unchanged by a move, so G_p (including the gcd(0,…,0)=0 convention) is preserved. The quoted passage merely asserts the Claim as 'standard' and explicitly omits its proof, and also does not state why equality of common-divisor sets for the changed pair implies invariance of the gcd of the whole N-tuple. Nothing in the text discharges this; the invariance of G_p is asserted, not argued.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Part (b) rests entirely on G_p being invariant (Step 4 applies it directly to get v_p(M) = gcd of initial valuations); with the Claim unproved, the choice-independence of M is unsupported as written.

parsed.notes: Part (a) (termination via product/#ones potential, plus at-least-one-survivor induction) is fully written and correct. Part (b) identifies the correct invariant G_p and the correct closed form for M, but the key invariance claim is explicitly deferred ('standard; details omitted'); the gap is the elementary Euclidean fact, trivially fixable but not written.
